body:
Self-Assembling Megastructure Materials. Materials and modular components that organize into larger structures under controlled conditions.

This database covers the technology as item 211 entry 24 of Manon's "100 Ultra-Advanced Future Technologies" catalog, section "Matter Manipulation and Molecular Manufacturing". It is the public edition: every factual claim below is drawn from real public science and engineering, honestly labeled.

Feasibility tier: experimentally supported. Self-assembly is proven from molecules (DNA origami) to modules (self-assembling robots); megastructure scale is unproven.

Classification: public database. This record profiles the technology; companion records cover known science, constraints, approaches, tools, unresolved problems, evidence, and outlook.

title: Self-Assembling Megastructure Materials - Known Science Foundations
description: Public edition: Materials and modular components that organize into larger structures under controlled conditions.
body:
Known science foundations of Self-Assembling Megastructure Materials.

DNA origami folds into designed shapes at the nanoscale. Programmable matter prototypes (MIT self-assembling cubes) and modular robots (M-TRAN, Roombots) reconfigure. 4D printing produces shape-changing structures. Scaling self-assembly to buildings or megastructures faces error-correction and energy limits.

Key quantity check (Largest modular-robot assemblies demonstrated / modules for a megastructure): computed ratio 1e-06 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.5. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

title: Self-Assembling Megastructure Materials - Physical and Engineering Constraints
description: Public edition: Materials and modular components that organize into larger structures under controlled conditions.
body:
Physical and engineering constraints on Self-Assembling Megastructure Materials.

Error rates compound with assembly size. Large structures need energy and material transport during assembly. Disassembly and repair of self-assembled megastructures are unsolved.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 11 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is megastructure module count vs assembly error rate at 11 orders of magnitude (megastructure module count larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.

title: Self-Assembling Megastructure Materials - Unresolved Problems
description: Public edition: Materials and modular components that organize into larger structures under controlled conditions.
body:
Unresolved problems for Self-Assembling Megastructure Materials, in priority order (research burden index 25, 2 blocking):

Scaling from modules to megastructures (severity 3/3, tractability 1/3, BLOCKING; priority 12).

Error correction in large assemblies (severity 3/3, tractability 2/3, BLOCKING; priority 9).

Reversible, repairable self-assembly (severity 2/3, tractability 2/3; priority 4).

These are open problems, stated plainly. A technology with unresolved blocking problems is not ready, whatever its promise.

body:
What would count as evidence of success for Self-Assembling Megastructure Materials:

Assembles 1,000 modules with <1% defects (weight 0.4; SATISFIED).

Self-assembles a load-bearing structure (weight 0.35; not yet satisfied).

Disassembles and reassembles on command (weight 0.25; not yet satisfied).
